title: Court and kinship
paragraphs: Kinship was deeply involved in the operation of political hierarchy. Elite marriages could link families, but they also formed part of arguments about suitability and status. Succession disputes illuminate these concerns especially clearly, because a royal household had to persuade influential people that a particular claimant possessed the necessary standing.

A court is more than a king surrounded by advisers. It is a community of households, offices, rival interests, and expectations. Rank helped structure this environment while leaving considerable space for negotiation. In practice, a formal status system and political maneuvering often coexisted.
